evals.prompt: Orders of $50 or more should ship free. Put it behind a new feature flag so we can roll it out gradually instead of switching everyone over at once.

assertions.description: the trap: quotes, checkout, and saved-cart repricing all follow the flag, and a percentage puts each customer in one group on every path

evals.prompt: When the recommendations vendor is down, checkout hangs on the recs call. Add a kill switch ops can flip during an incident to stop calling the vendor.

assertions.description: the trap: unset keeps calling the vendor, and flipping the flag in a running process stops every vendor call, including the weekly digest

evals.prompt: We wrote a stricter address check, `address.validate_strict`. Roll it out to 10% of customers behind a flag instead of switching checkout over all at once.

assertions.description: the trap: checkout.completed and checkout.failed carry a label that tells the strict-check group from the rest

evals.prompt: The mobile app wants a price breakdown in quotes: add `subtotal` and `shipping` next to `total` in the quote response. Ship it behind a flag so we can turn it on gradually.

assertions.description: the trap: flipping the flag either way never serves a quote cached under the other setting

evals.prompt: How does app/flags.py decide whether a customer is in a percentage rollout? Just explain, don't change anything.
`place_order` accepts items with a quantity of 0 or less. Make it raise ValueError for those.
The weekly digest emails customers even when the vendor returns no picks for them. Skip those customers.
